Title: UniSwarm: Unified Agent Swarming for Harnessing Collective Intelligence
Date: 2026-08-06
Summary: UniSwarm coordinates research-agent swarms through a unified interface and complements parallel thinking as a new axis of test-time scaling. We introduce UniSwarm-35B-A3B, trained on UniScientist data to act as both the main agent and a sub-agent, achieving competitive performance against frontier research agents.
HeaderImage: /static/images/frontierscience/uniswarm-logo.png


<style>
/* ============================================================
   UniSwarm Blog Styles — scoped with sw- prefix.
   A single blue family, varied only by depth. Evolved from the
   FrontierScience "scientific elegance" language toward a
   "schematic / blueprint" register: mono-forward spec blocks,
   layered orchestration diagrams, depth-graded blue callouts.
   ============================================================ */

@import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Crimson+Pro:ital,wght@0,300;0,400;0,500;0,600;0,700;1,300;1,400&family=DM+Sans:ital,wght@0,400;0,500;0,600;0,700;0,800;1,400&family=JetBrains+Mono:wght@400;500;600;700&display=swap');

:root {
    /* ---- one blue family, ten depths ---- */
    --sw-b950: #071122;
    --sw-b900: #0b1c3a;
    --sw-b800: #10254d;
    --sw-b700: #1e3a8a;
    --sw-b600: #1d4ed8;
    --sw-b500: #2563eb;
    --sw-b400: #3b82f6;
    --sw-b300: #60a5fa;
    --sw-b200: #93c5fd;
    --sw-b100: #bfdbfe;
    --sw-b50:  #eff6ff;
    /* within-family cool accent (still blue, cyan-leaning) */
    --sw-c700: #075985;
    --sw-c600: #0369a1;
    --sw-c500: #0ea5e9;

    /* ---- neutral ink & surfaces ---- */
    --sw-ink:       #0c1222;
    --sw-ink-soft:  #334155;
    --sw-ink-muted: #64748b;
    --sw-surface:        #ffffff;
    --sw-surface-raised: #f8fafc;
    --sw-surface-sunken: #f1f5f9;
    --sw-border:  #e2e8f0;
    --sw-border-blue: #dbe7fb;

    --sw-font-display: 'Crimson Pro', 'Georgia', serif;
    --sw-font-body: 'DM Sans', 'Segoe UI', sans-serif;
    --sw-font-mono: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace;

    --sw-r-sm: 8px;
    --sw-r-md: 14px;
    --sw-r-lg: 20px;
    --sw-shadow-sm: 0 1px 3px rgba(15,23,42,0.05), 0 1px 2px rgba(15,23,42,0.06);
    --sw-shadow-md: 0 6px 22px rgba(15,23,42,0.07), 0 2px 6px rgba(15,23,42,0.04);
    --sw-shadow-lg: 0 16px 48px rgba(29,78,216,0.10), 0 6px 16px rgba(15,23,42,0.05);
}

/* ---- page-local overrides of the base .markdown styles (this post only) ----
   The article is NOT wrapped in a container (a wrapping block element would stop
   Markdown from processing the section headings), so we retune the base classes
   directly. Flowing prose keeps the site's serif for kinship with UniScientist. */
.markdown h1 {
    font-family: var(--sw-font-display);
    font-weight: 700; font-style: normal;
    font-size: 2.4em; letter-spacing: 0.005em; line-height: 1.15;
    color: var(--sw-ink); margin: 6px 0 10px;
}
.markdown h2 {
    font-family: var(--sw-font-display);
    font-weight: 600; font-size: 1.9em; letter-spacing: 0.01em;
    color: var(--sw-ink); margin: 10px 0 4px; scroll-margin-top: 84px;
}
.markdown h3 {
    font-family: var(--sw-font-display);
    font-weight: 600; font-size: 1.22em; color: var(--sw-b800); margin: 22px 0 6px;
}
/* on-theme blue inline code, overriding the base Monokai chip on this page */
.markdown code {
    font-family: var(--sw-font-mono);
    font-size: 0.84em;
    background: var(--sw-b50);
    color: var(--sw-b700);
    padding: 0.12em 0.44em;
    border-radius: 6px;
    border: 1px solid var(--sw-border-blue);
}
.markdown pre code { background: transparent; border: none; color: inherit; padding: 0; }

/* ---- animations ---- */
@keyframes sw-fade-up { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(22px); } to { opacity: 1; transform: none; } }
@keyframes sw-pulse   { 0%,100% { opacity: 0.35; } 50% { opacity: 0.7; } }
@keyframes sw-dash    { to { stroke-dashoffset: -24; } }

.sw-reveal { opacity: 0; }
.sw-reveal.is-visible { animation: sw-fade-up 0.7s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1) forwards; }

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
    .sw-reveal, .sw-reveal.is-visible { animation: none !important; opacity: 1 !important; transform: none !important; }
}

/* ---- section rule (blueprint tick) ---- */
.sw-rule {
    border: none; height: 1px; margin: 54px 0;
    background: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent, var(--sw-border) 18%, var(--sw-b400) 50%, var(--sw-border) 82%, transparent);
    opacity: 0.6;
}
.sw-kicker {
    font-family: var(--sw-font-mono);
    font-size: 0.72em;
    letter-spacing: 0.22em;
    text-transform: uppercase;
    color: var(--sw-b500);
    font-weight: 600;
    display: block;
    margin-bottom: 6px;
}

/* ============================================================
   HERO
   ============================================================ */
.sw-hero {
    position: relative;
    text-align: center;
    padding: 26px 0 30px;
    margin-bottom: 6px;
    overflow: hidden;
}
.sw-hero::before {
    content: "";
    position: absolute; inset: -60px 0 auto 50%;
    transform: translateX(-50%);
    width: 720px; height: 520px;
    background:
        radial-gradient(circle at 50% 30%, rgba(37,99,235,0.09) 0%, rgba(14,165,233,0.04) 42%, transparent 70%);
    z-index: 0;
}
/* faint blueprint grid behind the hero */
.sw-hero::after {
    content: "";
    position: absolute; inset: 0;
    background-image:
        linear-gradient(to right, rgba(37,99,235,0.05) 1px, transparent 1px),
        linear-gradient(to bottom, rgba(37,99,235,0.05) 1px, transparent 1px);
    background-size: 34px 34px;
    -webkit-mask-image: radial-gradient(circle at 50% 34%, black, transparent 66%);
            mask-image: radial-gradient(circle at 50% 34%, black, transparent 66%);
    z-index: 0;
    pointer-events: none;
}
.sw-hero > * { position: relative; z-index: 1; }
.sw-lede {
    font-family: var(--sw-font-body);
    font-size: 1.08em; line-height: 1.78; color: var(--sw-ink-soft);
    max-width: 800px; margin: 0 auto 22px; text-align: left;
    animation: sw-fade-up 0.8s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1) both;
}
.sw-lede strong { color: var(--sw-ink); }
.sw-hero-chips { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 12px; justify-content: center; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 820px; }
.sw-hchip {
    flex: 1 1 200px; min-width: 178px; max-width: 262px;
    border: 1px solid var(--sw-border); border-top: 3px solid var(--sw-b500);
    border-radius: var(--sw-r-sm); background: var(--sw-surface);
    padding: 12px 15px; text-align: left; box-shadow: var(--sw-shadow-sm);
}
.sw-hchip b { display: block; font-family: var(--sw-font-body); font-weight: 700; font-size: 0.92em; color: var(--sw-b700); margin-bottom: 3px; }
.sw-hchip small { font-size: 0.8em; color: var(--sw-ink-muted); line-height: 1.5; }
.sw-hchip:nth-child(1) { border-top-color: var(--sw-b700); }
.sw-hchip:nth-child(2) { border-top-color: var(--sw-b500); }
.sw-hchip:nth-child(3) { border-top-color: var(--sw-c500); }
.sw-author { margin: 44px 0; }
.sw-author .sw-rule-slim { margin: 0; }
.sw-byline {
    text-align: center; font-family: var(--sw-font-mono);
    font-size: 0.82em; letter-spacing: 0.06em; color: var(--sw-b700); font-weight: 600;
    margin: 14px 0;
}

/* ============================================================
   ORCHESTRATION SCHEMATIC (hero concept diagram)
   ============================================================ */
.sw-figure { margin: 34px 0; }
.sw-figure-cap {
    font-size: 0.85em; color: var(--sw-ink-muted);
    text-align: center; margin-top: 14px; line-height: 1.6;
    font-style: italic;
}

.sw-dag {
    border: 1px solid var(--sw-border); border-radius: var(--sw-r-lg);
    max-height: 440px; overflow: auto; box-shadow: var(--sw-shadow-sm);
    background-image:
        linear-gradient(to right, rgba(37,99,235,0.05) 1px, transparent 1px),
        linear-gradient(to bottom, rgba(37,99,235,0.05) 1px, transparent 1px);
    background-size: 26px 26px; background-color: #fff;
    padding: 22px 18px;
}
.sw-dag-flow { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; min-width: 300px; }
.sw-dag-cap { font-family: var(--sw-font-mono); font-size: 0.8em; font-weight: 600; padding: 9px 18px; border-radius: 999px; }
.sw-dag-cap.q { background: var(--sw-b50); border: 1px solid var(--sw-border-blue); color: var(--sw-b700); }
.sw-dag-cap.ans { background: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--sw-b900), var(--sw-b700)); color: #eaf1ff; box-shadow: 0 8px 20px rgba(16,37,77,0.28); }
.sw-dag-arrow { color: var(--sw-b400); font-family: var(--sw-font-mono); font-size: 0.68em; margin: 8px 0; text-align: center; letter-spacing: 0.04em; }
.sw-dag-stage { width: 100%; max-width: 520px; border: 1px solid var(--sw-border-blue); border-radius: var(--sw-r-md); background: var(--sw-surface); padding: 12px 14px; box-shadow: var(--sw-shadow-sm); }
.sw-dag-main { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; flex-wrap: wrap; font-size: 0.9em; color: var(--sw-ink); font-weight: 600; }
.sw-dag-role { font-family: var(--sw-font-mono); font-size: 0.64em; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.08em; color: #fff; background: var(--sw-b700); padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 5px; }
.sw-dag-tool { margin-left: auto; font-family: var(--sw-font-mono); font-size: 0.68em; color: #eaf1ff; background: var(--sw-b600); padding: 3px 10px; border-radius: 999px; }
.sw-dag-tool::before { content: "\2699  "; opacity: 0.85; }
.sw-dag-subs { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 8px; margin-top: 10px; }
.sw-dag-sub { flex: 1 1 128px; border: 1px solid var(--sw-border); border-top: 3px solid var(--sw-b400); border-radius: var(--sw-r-sm); background: var(--sw-surface-raised); padding: 8px 10px; }
.sw-dag-sub b { font-family: var(--sw-font-mono); font-size: 0.76em; color: var(--sw-b700); display: block; }
.sw-dag-sub .sw-dag-goal { font-family: var(--sw-font-mono); font-size: 0.62em; color: var(--sw-ink-muted); }
.sw-dag-sub.dep { border-top-color: var(--sw-c500); flex-basis: 100%; }
.sw-dag-dep { font-family: var(--sw-font-mono); font-size: 0.64em; color: var(--sw-c700); background: #e6f4fb; border: 1px solid #cbe6f5; border-radius: 5px; padding: 1px 7px; display: inline-block; margin-top: 5px; }
.sw-dag-note { font-family: var(--sw-font-mono); font-size: 0.64em; color: var(--sw-ink-muted); margin-top: 9px; }
.sw-dag-kind { font-family: var(--sw-font-mono); font-size: 0.6em; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 999px; }
.sw-dag-kind.coop { background: var(--sw-b50); color: var(--sw-b700); border: 1px solid var(--sw-border-blue); }
.sw-dag-kind.comp { background: #e6f4fb; color: var(--sw-c700); border: 1px solid #cbe6f5; }
.sw-dag-kind.verify { background: var(--sw-b100); color: var(--sw-b800); border: 1px solid var(--sw-b200); }
.sw-dag-kind.integrate { background: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--sw-b800), var(--sw-b600)); color: #eaf1ff; }
.sw-dag-sub.win { border-top-color: var(--sw-b700); }

/* ============================================================
   SPEC BLOCK (the single tool, terminal-style)
   ============================================================ */
.sw-spec {
    border-radius: var(--sw-r-md);
    overflow: hidden;
    width: fit-content; max-width: 100%;
    margin: 26px auto;
    border: 1px solid var(--sw-border-blue);
    background: var(--sw-b950);
    box-shadow: var(--sw-shadow-sm);
}
.sw-spec .sw-spec-cap {
    font-family: var(--sw-font-mono); font-size: 0.68em; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase;
    color: #7f9bd0; padding: 12px 22px 0;
}
.sw-spec pre {
    margin: 0; padding: 12px 22px 20px;
    background: transparent;
    color: #d7e3fb;
    font-family: var(--sw-font-mono);
    font-size: 0.82em; line-height: 1.75;
    overflow-x: auto;
}
.sw-spec .k { color: #93c5fd; }          /* keys */
.sw-spec .s { color: #7dd3fc; }          /* strings */
.sw-spec .c { color: #6784b3; font-style: italic; }  /* comments */
.sw-spec .p { color: #cbd5e1; }          /* punctuation / plain */
.sw-spec .hl { color: #bfdbfe; font-weight: 700; }   /* the one switch */

/* ============================================================
   VERSUS PANELS (by-value vs by-reference)
   ============================================================ */
.sw-versus {
    display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 18px; margin: 30px 0;
}
@media (max-width: 720px) { .sw-versus { grid-template-columns: 1fr; } }
.sw-vpanel {
    border-radius: var(--sw-r-md);
    padding: 22px 22px 20px;
    position: relative;
}
.sw-vpanel.bad {
    border: 1px dashed #c3ccd9;
    background: var(--sw-surface-sunken);
}
.sw-vpanel.good {
    border: 1px solid var(--sw-b500);
    background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(37,99,235,0.05), rgba(37,99,235,0.02));
    box-shadow: var(--sw-shadow-sm);
}
.sw-vhead {
    font-family: var(--sw-font-mono); font-size: 0.76em; font-weight: 600;
    letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase;
    display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; margin-bottom: 10px;
}
.sw-vpanel.bad .sw-vhead { color: var(--sw-ink-muted); }
.sw-vpanel.good .sw-vhead { color: var(--sw-b600); }
.sw-vmark { width: 18px; height: 18px; border-radius: 50%; display: inline-grid; place-items: center; font-size: 0.8em; color: #fff; }
.sw-vpanel.bad .sw-vmark { background: #94a3b8; }
.sw-vpanel.good .sw-vmark { background: var(--sw-b500); }
.sw-vpanel h4 { font-family: var(--sw-font-display); font-size: 1.12em; color: var(--sw-ink); margin: 0 0 8px; }
.sw-vpanel p { font-size: 0.9em; margin: 0 0 8px; }
.sw-vpanel p:last-child { margin-bottom: 0; }

/* ============================================================
   CONTEXT LAYOUT (fixed injection order, depth-graded bands)
   ============================================================ */
.sw-ctx {
    border: 1px solid var(--sw-border);
    border-radius: var(--sw-r-md);
    overflow: hidden;
    width: fit-content; max-width: 100%;
    margin: 26px auto;
    box-shadow: var(--sw-shadow-sm);
}
.sw-ctx-band {
    padding: 14px 20px;
    display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 14px;
    border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.5);
}
.sw-ctx-band:last-child { border-bottom: none; }
.sw-ctx-band .sw-ctx-key { font-family: var(--sw-font-mono); font-size: 0.78em; font-weight: 600; white-space: nowrap; }
.sw-ctx-band .sw-ctx-desc { font-size: 0.88em; }
.sw-ctx-band:nth-child(1) { background: var(--sw-b700); }
.sw-ctx-band:nth-child(2) { background: var(--sw-b500); }
.sw-ctx-band:nth-child(3) { background: var(--sw-b300); }
.sw-ctx-band:nth-child(4) { background: var(--sw-b100); }
.sw-ctx-band:nth-child(1) .sw-ctx-key, .sw-ctx-band:nth-child(1) .sw-ctx-desc { color: #eaf1ff; }
.sw-ctx-band:nth-child(2) .sw-ctx-key, .sw-ctx-band:nth-child(2) .sw-ctx-desc { color: #f2f7ff; }
.sw-ctx-band:nth-child(3) .sw-ctx-key, .sw-ctx-band:nth-child(3) .sw-ctx-desc { color: #10254d; }
.sw-ctx-band:nth-child(4) .sw-ctx-key, .sw-ctx-band:nth-child(4) .sw-ctx-desc { color: #10254d; }
.sw-ctx-band .sw-ctx-opt { font-family: var(--sw-font-mono); font-size: 0.66em; opacity: 0.72; }

/* ============================================================
   VISION / PATTERN / FEATURE GRIDS
   ============================================================ */
.sw-grid-3 { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); gap: 18px; margin: 30px 0; }
.sw-grid-2 { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr); gap: 18px; margin: 30px 0; }
@media (max-width: 720px) { .sw-grid-3, .sw-grid-2 { grid-template-columns: 1fr; } }

.sw-card {
    border: 1px solid var(--sw-border);
    border-radius: var(--sw-r-md);
    background: var(--sw-surface);
    padding: 24px 22px;
    position: relative; overflow: hidden;
    display: flex; flex-direction: column;
    transition: transform 0.32s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), box-shadow 0.32s, border-color 0.32s;
}
.sw-card::before { content: ""; position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; right: 0; height: 3px; transition: height 0.3s; }
.sw-card:nth-child(1)::before { background: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--sw-b700), var(--sw-b500)); }
.sw-card:nth-child(2)::before { background: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--sw-b500), var(--sw-b300)); }
.sw-card:nth-child(3)::before { background: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--sw-b300), var(--sw-c500)); }
.sw-card:hover { transform: translateY(-4px); border-color: transparent; box-shadow: var(--sw-shadow-lg); }
.sw-card:hover::before { height: 4px; }
.sw-card .sw-card-idx { font-family: var(--sw-font-mono); font-size: 0.72em; color: var(--sw-b400); font-weight: 600; }
.sw-card h4 { font-family: var(--sw-font-body); font-size: 1.04em; font-weight: 700; color: var(--sw-ink); margin: 6px 0 10px; }
.sw-card p { font-size: 0.9em; color: var(--sw-ink-muted); margin: 0; line-height: 1.72; }

/* mini wiring diagram inside pattern cards */
.sw-wire {
    margin-top: auto; padding: 12px 14px;
    background: var(--sw-b950); border-radius: var(--sw-r-sm);
    font-family: var(--sw-font-mono); font-size: 0.72em; line-height: 1.7;
    color: #cfe0fb; overflow-x: auto; white-space: pre-wrap; word-break: break-word;
}
.sw-wire + .sw-wire { margin-top: 14px; }
.sw-wire .r { color: var(--sw-b300); }
.sw-wire .a { color: #eaf1ff; }
.sw-wire .d { color: #7dd3fc; }
.sw-wire .cm { color: #6784b3; }

/* ============================================================
   DARK INSIGHT BANNER
   ============================================================ */
.sw-banner {
    position: relative; overflow: hidden;
    background: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--sw-b950) 0%, var(--sw-b800) 55%, var(--sw-b900) 100%);
    border-radius: var(--sw-r-lg);
    padding: 34px 38px; margin: 40px 0;
    color: #e8eefb;
    box-shadow: 0 10px 34px rgba(11,28,58,0.34);
}
.sw-banner::before {
    content: ""; position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; right: 0; height: 1px;
    background: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent, rgba(96,165,250,0.5) 30%, rgba(14,165,233,0.5) 70%, transparent);
}
.sw-banner::after {
    content: ""; position: absolute; top: -55%; right: -12%;
    width: 380px; height: 380px; border-radius: 50%;
    background: radial-gradient(circle, rgba(37,99,235,0.16) 0%, rgba(14,165,233,0.07) 42%, transparent 70%);
    animation: sw-pulse 6s ease-in-out infinite;
}
.sw-banner .sw-kicker { color: var(--sw-b300); }
.sw-banner h3 { font-family: var(--sw-font-display); font-size: 1.3em; font-weight: 600; color: #eef3fd; margin: 0 0 14px; position: relative; z-index: 1; }
.sw-banner p { font-size: 0.96em; line-height: 1.85; color: #c7d5ee; margin: 0 0 10px; position: relative; z-index: 1; }
.sw-banner p:last-child { margin-bottom: 0; }
.sw-banner strong { color: #bfdbfe; }
.sw-banner em { color: #7dd3fc; font-style: normal; font-weight: 600; }

/* ============================================================
   FRAMED NOTE / BOX
   ============================================================ */
.sw-box {
    border: 1px solid var(--sw-border);
    border-radius: var(--sw-r-md);
    background: var(--sw-surface);
    padding: 26px 30px; margin: 30px 0;
    box-shadow: var(--sw-shadow-sm);
}
.sw-box h3 { font-family: var(--sw-font-display); font-size: 1.2em; font-weight: 600; color: var(--sw-ink); margin: 0 0 12px; }
.sw-box p { font-size: 0.94em; margin: 0 0 10px; }
.sw-box p:last-child { margin-bottom: 0; }
.sw-note {
    border-left: 4px solid var(--sw-b400);
    background: var(--sw-b50);
    border-radius: 0 var(--sw-r-sm) var(--sw-r-sm) 0;
    padding: 18px 22px; margin: 26px 0;
    font-size: 0.95em; color: var(--sw-ink-soft); line-height: 1.75;
}

/* ============================================================
   DATA AMPLIFIER (1 question -> 1 + N trajectories)
   ============================================================ */
.sw-amp {
    display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto 46px minmax(0, 1fr); align-items: center;
    gap: 0; margin: 28px auto; max-width: 720px;
    border: 1px solid var(--sw-border); border-radius: var(--sw-r-md);
    background: var(--sw-surface); padding: 22px 20px; box-shadow: var(--sw-shadow-sm);
}
@media (max-width: 640px) { .sw-amp { grid-template-columns: 1fr; gap: 14px; } }
.sw-amp-seed {
    text-align: center;
    background: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--sw-b900), var(--sw-b700));
    color: #eaf1ff; border-radius: var(--sw-r-sm); padding: 16px 18px;
    font-family: var(--sw-font-display);
}
.sw-amp-seed b { display: block; font-size: 1.5em; font-weight: 700; }
.sw-amp-seed span { font-family: var(--sw-font-mono); font-size: 0.66em; letter-spacing: 0.12em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--sw-b200); }
.sw-amp-arrow { position: relative; height: 2px; background: var(--sw-border-blue); }

Following the UniSwarm framework, we train Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on UniScientist data under one multi-task objective, releasing <strong>UniSwarm-35B-A3B</strong>: a single small model that serves as both the orchestrator and its sub-agents.</p>

# Harnessing a Swarm, Through One Tool

UniSwarm follows a <strong>centralized orchestration</strong> design. One main agent plans and coordinates the workflow; a swarm of sub-agents carries out the delegated work. The two roles are cleanly separated.

This centralization is deliberate, not merely for simplicity, but for <strong>error control</strong>. Every sub-agent result flows back through the main agent, which serves as a single validation bottleneck: it verifies, reconciles, and filters findings before they can influence the final synthesis. No sub-agent output reaches the answer unchecked. Recent work on scaling agent systems points the same way, architectures without centralized verification propagate errors more readily than those with centralized coordination (<a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.08296" class="sw-ref-link" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Kim et al., 2025</a>).

<div class="sw-figure sw-reveal">
<div class="sw-dag">
  <div class="sw-dag-flow">
    <div class="sw-dag-cap q">User question</div>
    <div class="sw-dag-arrow">↓</div>

    <div class="sw-dag-stage">
      <div class="sw-dag-main"><span class="sw-dag-role">MAIN</span> round 1 · decompose <span class="sw-dag-kind coop">cooperate</span> <span class="sw-dag-tool">swarm_run</span></div>
      <div class="sw-dag-subs">
        <div class="sw-dag-sub"><b>theory</b><span class="sw-dag-goal">derive the mechanism</span></div>
        <div class="sw-dag-sub"><b>experiment</b><span class="sw-dag-goal">design the assay</span></div>
        <div class="sw-dag-sub"><b>prior_art</b><span class="sw-dag-goal">survey prior results</span></div>
        <div class="sw-dag-sub"><b>data_survey</b><span class="sw-dag-goal">compile datasets</span></div>
      </div>
      <div class="sw-dag-note">division of labor: complementary facets run in parallel, independent</div>
    </div>
    <div class="sw-dag-arrow">↓&nbsp;&nbsp;outputs return to the main agent</div>

    <div class="sw-dag-stage">
      <div class="sw-dag-main"><span class="sw-dag-role">MAIN</span> round 2 · cross-check a key quantity <span class="sw-dag-kind comp">compete</span> <span class="sw-dag-tool">swarm_run</span></div>
      <div class="sw-dag-subs">
        <div class="sw-dag-sub"><b>closed_form</b><span class="sw-dag-goal">solve analytically</span></div>
        <div class="sw-dag-sub"><b>numerical</b><span class="sw-dag-goal">solve numerically</span></div>
        <div class="sw-dag-sub"><b>dimensional</b><span class="sw-dag-goal">dimensional estimate</span></div>
        <div class="sw-dag-sub"><b>from_scaling</b><span class="sw-dag-goal">estimate from scaling</span></div>
      </div>
      <div class="sw-dag-note">redundancy for reliability: the same quantity computed four ways, to be judged</div>
    </div>
    <div class="sw-dag-arrow">↓</div>

    <div class="sw-dag-stage">
      <div class="sw-dag-main"><span class="sw-dag-role">MAIN</span> round 3 · adjudicate &amp; stress-test <span class="sw-dag-kind verify">verify</span> <span class="sw-dag-tool">swarm_run</span></div>
      <div class="sw-dag-subs">
        <div class="sw-dag-sub dep"><b>judge</b><span class="sw-dag-dep">depends_on ← closed_form, numerical, dimensional, from_scaling</span></div>
        <div class="sw-dag-sub dep"><b>red_team</b><span class="sw-dag-dep">depends_on ← theory, experiment</span></div>
      </div>
      <div class="sw-dag-note">agreement across methods raises confidence; a red-team tries to break the result</div>
    </div>
    <div class="sw-dag-arrow">↓</div>

    <div class="sw-dag-stage">
      <div class="sw-dag-main"><span class="sw-dag-role">MAIN</span> round 4 · synthesize <span class="sw-dag-kind integrate">integrate</span> <span class="sw-dag-tool">swarm_run</span></div>
      <div class="sw-dag-subs">
        <div class="sw-dag-sub win dep"><b>integrator</b><span class="sw-dag-dep">depends_on ← *  (all completed sub-agents)</span></div>
      </div>
      <div class="sw-dag-note">fold the verified findings into one coherent result</div>
    </div>
    <div class="sw-dag-arrow">↓</div>
    <div class="sw-dag-cap ans">Final answer</div>
  </div>
</div>
<div class="sw-figure-cap">An illustrative run. The main agent orchestrates only through <code>swarm_run</code>: it cooperates across facets, competes on the load-bearing steps, verifies with a judge and a red-team, then integrates. Every sub-agent shares the same four tools (<code>search</code>, <code>visit</code>, <code>google_scholar</code>, <code>python_interpreter</code>); each node just shows its assigned goal. Dependencies point back to earlier rounds, so the run is a DAG whose layers are the rounds. Scroll to follow it.</div>
</div>

The main agent's job is decision, not execution: how to decompose the problem, which sub-agents to assign, what each should do, and how their results should be interpreted and integrated, with increasing precision across rounds. The sub-agents provide the capability. Each has web search (<code>search</code>), page visits (<code>visit</code>), Google Scholar (<code>google_scholar</code>), and a stateless Python interpreter (<code>python_interpreter</code>). Depending on its assignment, a sub-agent may investigate a topic, gather evidence, verify a claim, reproduce a calculation, critique an earlier result, or synthesize a line of reasoning, then return.

<hr class="sw-rule">

## Methodology

<p>Every design decision serves one of two goals, and usually both: <strong>keep the main agent's job small</strong>, and <strong>give each sub-agent enough context to act well</strong>. The main agent should not spend capacity picking tools or restating context it already holds. The sub-agent should never have to guess what it is part of or what its answer should rest on.</p>

### The orchestration model

A run starts from the user's question. At each step the main agent does one of two things: dispatch a batch of sub-agents, or emit a final answer and stop. Work proceeds in <strong>rounds</strong>, and each round is a single <code>swarm_run</code> call. A round carries an optional shared context and a list of sub-agent specifications; a specification is a unique id, the task, an optional role override, and an optional list of dependencies.

<div class="sw-note">
Sub-agents in the same round run in parallel and cannot see one another, so a dependency may point only to an <strong>earlier</strong> round. Dependencies therefore run backward across rounds, forming a directed acyclic graph whose layers <em>are</em> the rounds: a sub-agent can build on any earlier result, but never on a peer in its own batch. A dependency is expressed by splitting work across rounds.
</div>

### A single tool for every mode of work

A controller with many tools spends real capacity deciding which one to use, overhead that does not advance the problem. The main agent therefore has exactly one tool. Independent work, dependent work, verification, and integration all run through it. There is no separate tool and no mode flag: intent is expressed through <strong>how many</strong> sub-agents are spawned, <strong>what</strong> each is asked to do, and <strong>which</strong> ones are wired together.

<div class="sw-spec sw-reveal">
<div class="sw-spec-cap">swarm_run: the entire interface</div>
<pre><span class="c">// common case: a sub-agent is an id + a task</span>
<span class="k">swarm_run</span>(<span class="p">{</span>
  <span class="k">shared_context</span>: <span class="s">"…"</span><span class="p">,</span>     <span class="c">// shared batch background</span>
  <span class="k">agents</span>: <span class="p">[</span>
    <span class="p">{</span> <span class="k">agent_id</span>: <span class="s">"…"</span><span class="p">,</span>       <span class="c">// unique across the run</span>
      <span class="k">task</span>: <span class="s">"…"</span><span class="p">,</span>           <span class="c">// what this agent does</span>
      <span class="k">system_prompt</span>: <span class="s">"…"</span><span class="p">,</span>  <span class="c">// optional role override</span>
      <span class="hl">depends_on</span>: <span class="p">[</span><span class="s">"…"</span><span class="p">] }</span>  <span class="c">// the only behavioral switch</span>
  <span class="p">]</span>
<span class="p">}</span>)</pre>
</div>

One optional field, <code>depends_on</code>, is the entire difference between independent and dependent work. With it, the sub-agent builds on prior results; without it, it runs on its own. The tool itself does not change.

### Passing context by reference

The context model follows from one observation about model behavior. Take a common situation: a sub-agent returns a long report, often more than 8k tokens, and a later sub-agent needs it, say to verify it. Passing that report <em>by value</em> fails in two ways.

<div class="sw-versus sw-reveal">
  <div class="sw-vpanel bad">
    <div class="sw-vhead"><span class="sw-vmark">✗</span> By value, copy the report into the next task</div>
    <h4>Expensive <span style="font-weight:400">and</span> lossy</h4>
    <p><strong>Cost:</strong> the main agent must hold the entire 8k-token report in its own context and re-emit it verbatim as a tool argument, paying that cost again on every hand-off.</p>
    <p><strong>Fidelity:</strong> arguments this verbose almost never appear in training, so the main agent doesn't copy, it <em>compresses</em>, passing a heavily condensed summary. The downstream sub-agent then verifies only a lossy summary of what the round actually produced.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="sw-vpanel good">
    <div class="sw-vhead"><span class="sw-vmark">✓</span> By reference, write a short id</div>
    <h4>Cheap <span style="font-weight:400">and</span> faithful</h4>
    <p>The main agent writes only <code>depends_on: ["A"]</code>; the system splices in <code>A</code>'s <strong>full</strong> output before the next sub-agent starts. The data travels through the run, the main agent carries only the wiring.</p>
    <p>Its output per dispatch stays small and roughly <strong>constant</strong>, rather than growing with the size of the results it forwards. The downstream sub-agent verifies the real report, not a summary of it.</p>
  </div>
</div>

This layout is how each sub-agent's <strong>user prompt</strong> is assembled, in a fixed order, with each part present only when set. The <strong>system prompt</strong> is a separate, independent part that carries the sub-agent's role and tool-use rules:

<div class="sw-ctx sw-reveal">
  <div class="sw-ctx-band"><span class="sw-ctx-key">## [Original Question]</span><span class="sw-ctx-desc">the original question, always present</span></div>
  <div class="sw-ctx-band"><span class="sw-ctx-key">## [Shared Context]</span><span class="sw-ctx-desc">batch-level background <span class="sw-ctx-opt">(if shared_context set)</span></span></div>
  <div class="sw-ctx-band"><span class="sw-ctx-key">## [Upstream Agent Outputs]</span><span class="sw-ctx-desc">full outputs of referenced agents, spliced by reference <span class="sw-ctx-opt">(if depends_on set)</span></span></div>
  <div class="sw-ctx-band"><span class="sw-ctx-key">## [Your Task]</span><span class="sw-ctx-desc">this sub-agent's own task</span></div>
</div>

Reference resolution is strict: <code>["*"]</code> inherits every completed, successful sub-agent, the natural form for a final integrator. A reference to an unknown agent is rejected; a reference to a <em>failed</em> agent is rejected too, since downstream work should not build on a failure. The same ids that make context cheap to move also lay down an explicit propagation chain between sub-agents, giving the orchestration a more structured form.

### Shared context, stated once

<code>shared_context</code> complements <code>depends_on</code> and follows the same principle: the main agent should not write the same context twice. Background common to the batch, established facts, constraints, the scenario, is stated once and injected into every sub-agent. It is not limited to fixed setup: as the run advances, the main agent can place into it what has already been established and the stage the work has reached, so each new batch starts from the current state instead of from scratch.

<div class="sw-note">
This matters most for <strong>competition</strong>, which dispatches many sub-agents on the same task with the same background. Without a shared channel, the main agent would repeat that background in every task. With <code>shared_context</code>, the background is stated once, and each task carries only what differs, the method, the assumption, or the framing.
</div>

### Cooperation, competition, and their hybrid

Neither cooperation nor competition is a separate mode; both are patterns of how sub-agents are dispatched and wired.

<div class="sw-grid-3 sw-reveal">
  <div class="sw-card">
    <span class="sw-card-idx">01 · division of labor</span>
    <h4>Cooperation</h4>
    <p>The problem is split into complementary parts, one sub-agent runs each, and a single integrator closes the round. Parallel outputs are never left unmerged.</p>
    <div class="sw-wire"><span class="r">R1</span> <span class="a">theory · experiment · prior_art</span>
<span class="r">R2</span> <span class="a">integrator</span> <span class="d">depends_on ["*"]</span></div>
  </div>
  <div class="sw-card">
    <span class="sw-card-idx">02 · redundancy for reliability</span>
    <h4>Competition</h4>
    <p>Several sub-agents run the same task, each with a different method, assumption, or framing. A judge weighs agreement against divergence. The number of competitors scales with the stakes.</p>
    <div class="sw-wire"><span class="r">R1</span> <span class="a">closed-form · numerical · estimate · scaling</span>
<span class="r">R2</span> <span class="a">judge</span> <span class="d">depends_on [the four]</span></div>
  </div>
  <div class="sw-card">
    <span class="sw-card-idx">03 · the default for hard problems</span>
    <h4>Hybrid</h4>
    <p>Cooperate across facets and compete within each. Split into tracks, run a few competitors inside each, judge every track, integrate the winners, breadth and reliability in a single pass.</p>
    <div class="sw-wire"><span class="cm">// per track: compete → judge</span>
<span class="r">R1</span> <span class="a">track×competitors</span>
<span class="r">R2</span> <span class="a">judge/track</span> → <span class="a">integrate winners</span></div>
  </div>
</div>

None of this is a fixed recipe. The main agent composes these patterns freely, over as many rounds as the problem needs, and revises the plan as results come in. The verification patterns are just dispatch patterns too, evidence → draft → review → revision; deriving a quantity two ways and reconciling them; a red-team sub-agent tasked only with breaking a conclusion, followed by a referee; a shallow pass to map the terrain, then deeper sub-agents aimed at the weak spots. Only the wiring changes.

### Failure semantics

Sub-agents fail independently. A malformed specification produces an error result on its own, and the rest of the batch runs to completion. A sub-agent that crashes or exhausts its turn budget is marked failed rather than allowed to abort the round. A single bad sub-agent never brings down the call.

<div class="sw-note">
Partial failure is expected rather than exceptional, a form of feedback from the environment, more common as that environment grows less stable: a search times out, a page fails to load, a computation runs past its budget. The batch keeps what succeeded, and the main agent decides how to handle what did not.
</div>

<hr class="sw-rule">

## Swarm Training

The methodology defines an interface. A model still has to learn to use it well: when to decompose, how many competitors to run, which results to trust, when to stop. We teach this with <strong>agentic supervised fine-tuning</strong> on trajectories the swarm produces when driven by a strong model.

### Collecting agent trajectories, the swarm as a data amplifier

We run the full swarm with a strong reasoning model (DeepSeek-V4-Pro) driving both roles, on <strong>4,000 hard research questions</strong> drawn from UniScientist (<a href="/blog/UniScientist" class="sw-ref-link">UniPat AI, 2026</a>), sampled uniformly across physics, chemistry, biology, and mathematics. Each run produces two kinds of trajectory:

<div class="sw-amp sw-reveal">
  <div class="sw-amp-seed"><span>one question</span><b>1</b>hard, decomposable</div>
  <div class="sw-amp-arrow"></div>
  <div class="sw-amp-out">
    <div class="sw-amp-row mainrole"><span class="sw-amp-n">1×</span><span class="sw-amp-l"><strong>orchestration trajectory</strong>, the rounds dispatched, and how results were integrated</span></div>
    <div class="sw-amp-row subrole"><span class="sw-amp-n">N×</span><span class="sw-amp-l"><strong>research trajectories</strong>, each sub-agent's searches, visits, and computations for a distinct subproblem</span></div>
  </div>
</div>

This makes the swarm an unusually data-efficient source of supervision. A single question expands into one orchestration trajectory plus many research trajectories, each a distinct subproblem. A modest pool of questions produces a large and diverse training set, and the multiplier is highest on <strong>hard, decomposable problems</strong>, exactly the ones where good trajectories are otherwise scarce.

<div class="sw-stats sw-reveal">
  <div class="sw-stat"><div class="sw-stat-label">UniScientist Query-Rubrics</div><div class="sw-stat-num">4,000</div><div class="sw-stat-note">hard research problems</div></div>
  <div class="sw-stat"><div class="sw-stat-label">Domains</div><div class="sw-stat-num">4</div><div class="sw-stat-note">physics · chem · bio · math</div></div>
  <div class="sw-stat"><div class="sw-stat-label">Roles per Model</div><div class="sw-stat-num">2</div><div class="sw-stat-note">orchestrator + sub-agent</div></div>
  <div class="sw-stat"><div class="sw-stat-label">Trajectories / Question</div><div class="sw-stat-num">1 + N</div><div class="sw-stat-note">one main, many research</div></div>
</div>

### Rejection sampling

The collected trajectories are not all worth learning from. We filter on two axes before training.

<div class="sw-grid-2 sw-reveal">
  <div class="sw-card">
    <span class="sw-card-idx">axis 1</span>
    <h4>Correctness</h4>
    <p>The main agent's final report is scored against per-question rubrics by a judge model. A trajectory whose final answer is wrong or weakly supported is rejected, so the model does not learn from confident but incorrect orchestration.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="sw-card">
    <span class="sw-card-idx">axis 2</span>
    <h4>Format &amp; tool-call integrity</h4>
    <p>A trajectory is rejected if any turn contains a malformed tool call, a hallucinated tool name, arguments that do not parse, an empty reasoning block, or a response not paired with its call. These errors are cheap to detect and disproportionately harmful to imitate: one bad call format learned in training reappears at inference and breaks the run.</p>
  </div>
</div>

What survives is a pool of clean, correct trajectories, main and sub together.

### Mixing roles: multi-task agentic SFT

At inference the same base model plays both roles; the role is selected by the system prompt. Because one model serves both, we train it on both distributions at once, main and sub trajectories pooled and fine-tuned together, as a single multi-task objective.

<div class="sw-roles sw-reveal">
  <div class="sw-role-col">
    <h4>MAIN · main-agent</h4>
    <ul>
      <li>decompose the problem into rounds</li>
      <li>delegate, wire dependencies, and compete</li>
      <li>verify pivotal claims; integrate what returns</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
  <div class="sw-role-hinge"><span>same base model<br>flexible roles</span></div>
  <div class="sw-role-col">
    <h4>SUB · sub-agent</h4>
    <ul>
      <li>gather evidence via search / visit / scholar</li>
      <li>compute and verify with Python</li>
      <li>return a self-contained deliverable + self-assessment</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>

The two roles pair naturally. Orchestration and research share a substrate, decompose, delegate, gather evidence, verify, integrate. Training them together lets that substrate reinforce from both directions, while the system prompt keeps the tool interfaces distinct. The result is one model that can both orchestrate the swarm and serve as its sub-agents.

<hr class="sw-rule">

## Results

We evaluate UniSwarm on four benchmark suites: <strong>FrontierScience</strong> (Olympiad and Research tracks; <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.21165" class="sw-ref-link" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Wang et al., 2026</a>), <strong>DeepResearch Bench II</strong> (<a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.08536" class="sw-ref-link" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Li et al., 2026</a>), <strong>ResearchRubrics</strong> (<a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.07685" class="sw-ref-link" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Sharma et al., 2025</a>), and <strong>Humanity's Last Exam</strong> (<a href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.14249" class="sw-ref-link" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Phan et al., 2025</a>). Only FrontierScience-Research is in-distribution; the others are out-of-distribution and measure how well the learned orchestration transfers. On FrontierScience, every baseline uses the same four-tool deep-research design as UniSwarm and runs at maximum thinking effort. "Aggr@4" combines four independent runs into one answer (<a href="/blog/UniScientist" class="sw-ref-link">UniPat AI, 2026</a>), a parallel-thinking form of test-time scaling applied <em>on top of</em> the swarm. On Humanity's Last Exam, all models run with tools; DeepSeek-V4-Pro and UniSwarm-35B-A3B are evaluated on the text subset while the others use the full set, and Claude-Fable-5 additionally runs with fallback.

<div class="sw-legend">
  <span><i class="ours"></i> UniSwarm-35B-A3B</span>
  <span><i class="aggr"></i> UniSwarm (Aggr@4)</span>
  <span><i class="base"></i> Baselines</span>
</div>

<div class="sw-chart-wrap sw-reveal">
  <canvas id="sw-results-canvas" aria-label="UniSwarm benchmark results across four suites"></canvas>
</div>

<script>
(function() {
    const canvas = document.getElementById("sw-results-canvas");
    if (!canvas || canvas.dataset.rendered === "1") return;
    canvas.dataset.rendered = "1";

    const sections = [
        {
            title: "FrontierScience-Research  ·  in-distribution",
            min: 0, max: 70,
            bars: [
                { name: "UniSwarm-35B-A3B (Aggr@4)", score: 65.0, ours: true, aggr: true },
                { name: "Claude-Opus-5", score: 58.3 },
                { name: "Kimi-K3", score: 55.0 },
                { name: "UniSwarm-35B-A3B", score: 53.3, ours: true },
                { name: "GPT-5.5", score: 51.7 },
                { name: "DeepSeek-V4-Pro", score: 51.7 },
                { name: "Claude-Opus-4.8", score: 48.3 },
                { name: "GLM-5.2", score: 43.3 },
                { name: "Seed-2.1-Pro", score: 40.0 },
                { name: "Qwen-3.7-Max", score: 36.7 },
                { name: "Gemini-3.6-Flash", score: 36.7 },
                { name: "Gemini-3.1-Pro", score: 23.3 }
            ]
        },
        {
            title: "FrontierScience-Olympiad  ·  out-of-distribution",
            min: 0, max: 95,
            bars: [
                { name: "UniSwarm-35B-A3B", score: 87.0, ours: true },
                { name: "DeepSeek-V4-Pro", score: 87.0 },
                { name: "Seed-2.1-Pro", score: 85.0 },
                { name: "Kimi-K3", score: 84.0 },
                { name: "Gemini-3.6-Flash", score: 84.0 },
                { name: "Gemini-3.1-Pro", score: 82.0 },
                { name: "Qwen-3.7-Max", score: 78.0 },
                { name: "GPT-5.5", score: 77.0 },
                { name: "Claude-Opus-4.8", score: 77.0 },
                { name: "GLM-5.2", score: 77.0 }
            ]
        },
        {
            title: "DeepResearch Bench II  ·  out-of-distribution",
            min: 0, max: 70,
            bars: [
                { name: "UniSwarm-35B-A3B", score: 61.5, ours: true },
                { name: "iFlow-Researcher", score: 60.0 },
                { name: "OpenAI-o3 Deep Research", score: 45.4 },
                { name: "Gemini-3-Pro Deep Research", score: 44.6 },
                { name: "Doubao Deep Research", score: 41.0 },
                { name: "Grok Deep Search", score: 39.2 }
            ]
        },
        {
            title: "ResearchRubrics  ·  out-of-distribution",
            min: 0, max: 85,
            bars: [
                { name: "UniSwarm-35B-A3B", score: 76.0, ours: true },
                { name: "GPT-5.6-Sol", score: 73.8 },
                { name: "Claude-Opus-4.8", score: 73.5 },
                { name: "GLM-5.2", score: 71.1 },
                { name: "Step 3.5 Flash", score: 65.3 },
                { name: "Gemini DeepResearch", score: 61.5 }
            ]
        },
        {
            title: "Humanity's Last Exam  ·  out-of-distribution",
            min: 0, max: 70,
            bars: [
                { name: "Claude-Fable-5", score: 63.0 },
                { name: "UniSwarm-35B-A3B", score: 60.0, ours: true },
                { name: "GPT-5.6 Sol", score: 58.0 },
                { name: "Claude-Opus-4.8", score: 57.9 },
                { name: "Kimi-K3", score: 56.0 },
                { name: "GPT-5.5", score: 52.2 },
                { name: "DeepSeek-V4-Pro", score: 48.2 }
            ]
        }
    ];

    const S = {
        baseW: 900, rowH: 33, sectionGap: 24, headGap: 30,
        padX: 26, labelW: 232, scoreW: 50, trackH: 14, hover: null, targets: []
    };
    const LABEL_FONT_B = "700 12.5px 'DM Sans', Arial, sans-serif";
    const LABEL_FONT   = "12.5px 'DM Sans', Arial, sans-serif";

    const rr = (ctx, x, y, w, h, r) => {
        const rad = Math.max(0, Math.min(r, w / 2, h / 2));
        ctx.beginPath();
        ctx.moveTo(x + rad, y);
        ctx.arcTo(x + w, y, x + w, y + h, rad);
        ctx.arcTo(x + w, y + h, x, y + h, rad);
        ctx.arcTo(x, y + h, x, y, rad);
        ctx.arcTo(x, y, x + w, y, rad);
        ctx.closePath(); ctx.fill();
    };

    const baseH = () => {
        let y = 18;
        for (let i = 0; i < sections.length; i++) {
            y += S.headGap + sections[i].bars.length * S.rowH + S.sectionGap;
        }
        return y + 4;
    };

    // fixed left margin: tick (4) + gap (12) from the card edge
    const tick = 4, gap = 12;

    const render = () => {
        const bw = S.baseW, bh = baseH();
        const targetW = Math.min(bw, canvas.parentElement.clientWidth || bw);
        const scale = targetW / bw;
        const dpr = Math.max(2, window.devicePixelRatio || 2);
        canvas.style.width = Math.round(bw * scale) + "px";
        canvas.style.height = Math.round(bh * scale) + "px";
        canvas.width = Math.round(bw * scale * dpr);
        canvas.height = Math.round(bh * scale * dpr);
        S.scale = scale; S.targets = [];

        const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
        ctx.setTransform(dpr * scale, 0, 0, dpr * scale, 0, 0);
        ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = true; ctx.imageSmoothingQuality = "high";

        // pure-white canvas
        ctx.fillStyle = "#ffffff"; rr(ctx, 0, 0, bw, bh, 14);

        // measure the widest label so names never overlap the track
        const cardPad = 22;                 // inner-left padding of each section card
        const L = S.padX + cardPad + tick + gap;   // where labels + titles start
        ctx.font = LABEL_FONT_B;
        let maxLabel = 0;
        for (const s of sections) for (const b of s.bars) maxLabel = Math.max(maxLabel, ctx.measureText(b.name).width);
        S.labelW = Math.min(300, Math.max(170, Math.ceil(maxLabel) + 16));
        const trackX = L + S.labelW;
        S.trackW = bw - trackX - S.scoreW - (S.padX + cardPad);

        const trackH = S.trackH;
        let y = 18;
        for (let i = 0; i < sections.length; i++) {
            const s = sections[i];
            const secTop = y;
            const secH = S.headGap + s.bars.length * S.rowH + 12;

            // subtle premium section card: near-white fill + hairline border
            ctx.fillStyle = "#fcfdff";
            rr(ctx, S.padX, secTop, bw - S.padX * 2, secH, 12);
            ctx.strokeStyle = "#eaeef4"; ctx.lineWidth = 1;
            ctx.strokeRect(S.padX + 0.5, secTop + 0.5, bw - S.padX * 2 - 1, secH - 1);

            // title row: blue tick + name, with a muted distribution suffix
            const titleY = secTop + 22;
            const parts = s.title.split("·");
            const main = parts[0].trim();
            const suffix = parts[1] ? parts[1].trim() : "";
            ctx.fillStyle = "#1d4ed8";
            rr(ctx, S.padX + cardPad, titleY - 11, tick, 15, 2);
            ctx.textAlign = "left";
            ctx.fillStyle = "#0f1e3a"; ctx.font = "700 15px 'DM Sans', Arial, sans-serif";
            ctx.fillText(main, L, titleY);
            if (suffix) {
                const mw = ctx.measureText(main).width;
                ctx.fillStyle = "#9aa7bb"; ctx.font = "500 12px 'DM Sans', Arial, sans-serif";
                ctx.fillText("·  " + suffix, L + mw + 12, titleY);
            }

            const barsTop = secTop + S.headGap;
            for (let j = 0; j < s.bars.length; j++) {
                const b = s.bars[j];
                const rowY = barsTop + j * S.rowH;
                const trackY = rowY + (S.rowH - trackH) / 2;
                const cy = trackY + trackH / 2 + 4;
                const ratio = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, (b.score - s.min) / (s.max - s.min)));
                const fillW = Math.max(6, S.trackW * ratio);
                const tier = b.aggr ? "aggr" : (b.ours ? "ours" : "base");

                // label
                ctx.textAlign = "left";
                ctx.font = b.ours ? LABEL_FONT_B : LABEL_FONT;
                ctx.fillStyle = tier === "aggr" ? "#1e3a8a" : tier === "ours" ? "#2563eb" : "#475569";
                ctx.fillText(b.name, L, cy);

                // track (light-gray pill with a hairline for definition)
                ctx.fillStyle = "#eef1f6";
                rr(ctx, trackX, trackY, S.trackW, trackH, trackH / 2);
                ctx.strokeStyle = "#e4e8f0"; ctx.lineWidth = 1;
                ctx.beginPath();
                const rH = trackH / 2;
                ctx.moveTo(trackX + rH, trackY + 0.5);
                ctx.arcTo(trackX + S.trackW - 0.5, trackY + 0.5, trackX + S.trackW - 0.5, trackY + trackH - 0.5, rH);
                ctx.arcTo(trackX + S.trackW - 0.5, trackY + trackH - 0.5, trackX + rH, trackY + trackH - 0.5, rH);
                ctx.arcTo(trackX + 0.5, trackY + trackH - 0.5, trackX + 0.5, trackY + 0.5, rH);
                ctx.arcTo(trackX + 0.5, trackY + 0.5, trackX + rH, trackY + 0.5, rH);
                ctx.stroke();

                // subtle glow behind our bars
                if (b.ours) {
                    ctx.fillStyle = tier === "aggr" ? "rgba(30,58,138,0.10)" : "rgba(37,99,235,0.10)";
                    rr(ctx, trackX, trackY - 3, fillW, trackH + 6, (trackH + 6) / 2);
                }

                // fill
                const g = ctx.createLinearGradient(trackX, 0, trackX + fillW, 0);
                if (tier === "aggr") { g.addColorStop(0, "#152c66"); g.addColorStop(1, "#1e3a8a"); }
                else if (tier === "ours") { g.addColorStop(0, "#3b82f6"); g.addColorStop(1, "#2563eb"); }
                else { g.addColorStop(0, "#cdd6e3"); g.addColorStop(1, "#aab6c8"); }
                ctx.fillStyle = g;
                rr(ctx, trackX, trackY, fillW, trackH, trackH / 2);

                if (S.hover && S.hover.si === i && S.hover.bi === j) {
                    ctx.strokeStyle = tier === "base" ? "rgba(148,163,184,0.6)" : "rgba(37,99,235,0.55)";
                    ctx.lineWidth = 1.4;
                    ctx.strokeRect(trackX - 1.5, trackY - 1.5, S.trackW + 3, trackH + 3);
                }

                // score value
                ctx.fillStyle = tier === "aggr" ? "#1e3a8a" : tier === "ours" ? "#2563eb" : "#64748b";
                ctx.font = b.ours ? "700 12.5px 'JetBrains Mono', monospace" : "12px 'JetBrains Mono', monospace";
                ctx.fillText(b.score.toFixed(1), trackX + S.trackW + 9, cy);

                S.targets.push({ si: i, bi: j, x: trackX, y: trackY, w: S.trackW, h: trackH, name: b.name, score: b.score, tier });
            }
            y += S.headGap + s.bars.length * S.rowH + S.sectionGap;
        }

        // tooltip
        if (S.hover) {
            const t = S.targets.find(v => v.si === S.hover.si && v.bi === S.hover.bi);
            if (t) {
                const l1 = t.name, l2 = "Score  " + t.score.toFixed(1);
                ctx.font = "600 13px 'DM Sans', Arial, sans-serif";
                const w1 = ctx.measureText(l1).width;
                ctx.font = "700 13px 'JetBrains Mono', monospace";
                const w2 = ctx.measureText(l2).width;
                const bw2 = Math.max(w1, w2) + 24, bh2 = 50;
                let bx = Math.max(16, Math.min(S.baseW - bw2 - 16, t.x + t.w * 0.4));
                let by = Math.max(10, t.y - bh2 - 8);
                ctx.save();
                ctx.shadowColor = "rgba(15,23,42,0.18)"; ctx.shadowBlur = 12; ctx.shadowOffsetY = 4;
                ctx.fillStyle = "rgba(255,255,255,0.98)"; rr(ctx, bx, by, bw2, bh2, 9);
                ctx.restore();
                ctx.strokeStyle = "rgba(148,163,184,0.4)"; ctx.lineWidth = 1;
                ctx.strokeRect(bx + 0.5, by + 0.5, bw2 - 1, bh2 - 1);
                ctx.textAlign = "left";
                ctx.fillStyle = "#0f172a"; ctx.font = "600 13px 'DM Sans', Arial, sans-serif";
                ctx.fillText(l1, bx + 12, by + 20);
                ctx.fillStyle = t.tier === "aggr" ? "#1e3a8a" : t.tier === "ours" ? "#2563eb" : "#475569";
                ctx.font = "700 13px 'JetBrains Mono', monospace";
                ctx.fillText(l2, bx + 12, by + 39);
            }
        }
    };

    render();
    window.addEventListener("resize", render, { passive: true });

    const hit = (evt) => {
        const rect = canvas.getBoundingClientRect();
        const x = (evt.clientX - rect.left) / Math.max(0.0001, S.scale);
        const y = (evt.clientY - rect.top) / Math.max(0.0001, S.scale);
        for (let i = S.targets.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
            const t = S.targets[i];
            if (x >= t.x && x <= t.x + t.w && y >= t.y - 4 && y <= t.y + t.h + 4) return { si: t.si, bi: t.bi };
        }
        return null;
    };
    canvas.addEventListener("mousemove", (e) => {
        const n = hit(e);
        const same = S.hover && n && S.hover.si === n.si && S.hover.bi === n.bi;
        if (!same) { S.hover = n; canvas.style.cursor = n ? "pointer" : "default"; render(); }
    }, { passive: true });
    canvas.addEventListener("mouseleave", () => { if (S.hover) { S.hover = null; render(); } }, { passive: true });
})();
</script>

<div class="sw-findings sw-reveal">
<h3>Key finding</h3>
<p>A small model trained on <strong>UniScientist</strong> data inside the UniSwarm framework is <strong>highly competitive with frontier deep-research agents many times its size</strong>, across every benchmark tested.</p>
</div>
